title: Haggai Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Haggai chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Haggai Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Haggai Chapter 2.

questions.question: On what day of the seventh month did the word of the LORD come by the prophet Haggai?
questions.correctAnswer: The one and twentieth day
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:1 states that the word of the LORD came in the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month.

questions.question: To whom did the LORD command Haggai to speak in Haggai 2:2?
options: Zerubbabel and Joshua and the residue of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Zerubbabel and Joshua and the residue of the people
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:2 directs Haggai to speak to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, Joshua the son of Josedech, and the residue of the people.

questions.question: What question did the LORD ask about the house's former glory?
options: Is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?
How long will the house last?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:3 asks, 'Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?'

questions.question: What encouragement does the LORD give Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people in verse 4?
options: Be strong and work, for I am with you
Rest and wait for my command
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and work, for I am with you
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:4 says, 'Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel... and work: for I am with you, saith the LORD of hosts.'

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:5, what remains among the people as it was when they came out of Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: God's spirit
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:5 states, 'so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD says He will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:6 states, 'Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land.'

questions.question: What will come as the LORD shakes all nations according to Haggai 2:7?
questions.correctAnswer: The desire of all nations
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:7 says, 'And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come.'

questions.question: Who does the LORD claim ownership of silver and gold?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:8 states, 'The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.'

questions.question: True or False: The glory of the latter house will be less than the former house.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:9 says, 'The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former.'

questions.question: In Haggai 2, which of the following instructions comes first?
options: Be strong and work for God is with you
Inquire of the priests about the law
Consider from the day the foundation was laid
Speak to Zerubbabel about shaking the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and work for God is with you
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:4 gives the first instruction to be strong and work, before instructions in verses 11, 15, and 21.

questions.question: True or False: Haggai was commanded to ask the priests about the holiness of eating certain foods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:11-12 concerns asking the priests about the law regarding holy flesh touching bread and other foods, not about eating.

questions.question: Who is described as the governor of Judah in Haggai 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Zerubbabel
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:2 identifies Zerubbabel as the son of Shealtiel and governor of Judah.

questions.question: What will the LORD give in the place of the house according to Haggai 2:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:9 says, 'and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD says to fear because He will not be with the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:5 says, 'so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not.' indicating the LORD's presence and a command not to fear.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:3, how do the people now see the house compared to its first glory?
questions.correctAnswer: As nothing in comparison
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:3 asks, 'is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?' referring to how the house is now seen compared to its former glory.

medium.title: Haggai Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Haggai Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:9, what does the LORD promise about the glory of the latter house compared to the former?
options: The glory of the latter house shall be less than the former
The glory of the latter house shall be equal to the former
The glory of the latter house shall be greater than the former
The latter house will have no glory
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of the latter house shall be greater than the former
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:9 explicitly states that the glory of the latter house shall be greater than that of the former, and the LORD will give peace in this place.

questions.question: What is the significance of the date mentioned in Haggai 2:10 when the word of the LORD came to Haggai?
options: It was the first day of the year
It was the four and twentieth day of the ninth month in the second year of Darius
It was the day the temple was completed
It was the day Zerubbabel was appointed governor
questions.correctAnswer: It was the four and twentieth day of the ninth month in the second year of Darius
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:10 specifies the exact date and historical context, indicating the LORD’s word came on the 24th day of the ninth month in Darius's second year, grounding the prophecy historically.

questions.question: What question does the LORD instruct Haggai to ask the priests in Haggai 2:11?
options: Whether the temple will be rebuilt
About the law concerning holy flesh touching common food
If Zerubbabel will be a good leader
questions.correctAnswer: About the law concerning holy flesh touching common food
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:11 directs Haggai to ask the priests about the law on whether holy flesh touching bread or other food makes it holy, connecting to ritual purity.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:12, if holy flesh touches bread, wine, or oil, does the touched food become holy?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:12 states that the priests answered 'No' to the question whether food touched by holy flesh becomes holy, indicating holiness is not transferred by contact.

questions.question: Based on Haggai 2:13, if a person unclean by touching a dead body touches food, will the food become unclean?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:13 shows the priests affirm that food touched by someone unclean by a dead body does become unclean, emphasizing the transmission of uncleanness.

questions.question: What does Haggai say about the people and their offerings in Haggai 2:14?
options: Their offerings are accepted and pleasing
Their offerings are unclean before the LORD
Their offerings are more holy than before
questions.correctAnswer: Their offerings are unclean before the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:14 explains that the people and their works are unclean before the LORD, and what they offer is also unclean, indicating a spiritual problem affecting their worship.

questions.question: How does Haggai 2:15 encourage the people to reflect on their situation?
options: To forget the past and focus on the future
To consider their condition from the moment before the temple foundation was laid
To compare their current temple to Solomon’s temple
To ask for forgiveness for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: To consider their condition from the moment before the temple foundation was laid
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:15 calls the people to consider their state starting from before any stone was laid on the temple, encouraging reflection on their hardships and God's timing.

questions.question: In Haggai 2:16, what two examples illustrate the people's reduced productivity since the temple foundation days?
options: Harvesting twenty measures yielding twenty, and drawing fifty vessels yielding fifty
Harvesting twenty measures yielding ten, and drawing fifty vessels yielding twenty
Harvesting ten measures yielding twenty, and drawing twenty vessels yielding fifty
Harvesting fifty measures yielding fifty, and drawing twenty vessels yielding ten
questions.correctAnswer: Harvesting twenty measures yielding ten, and drawing fifty vessels yielding twenty
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:16 contrasts expectation with reality: twenty measures yielded only ten and fifty vessels yielded twenty, showing diminished blessings linked to their disobedience.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give in Haggai 2:17 for the people’s hardships despite His judgments?
options: They repented and turned to Him
They ignored His judgments and did not return to Him
They were punished because of their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They ignored His judgments and did not return to Him
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:17 states that although the LORD smote them with various judgments, they did not turn to Him, explaining the continuation of their hardships.

questions.question: How does Haggai 2:18 instruct the people to consider their condition moving forward?
options: From the day the temple will be completed
From the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid
From the day they left Egypt
From the day Zerubbabel became governor
questions.correctAnswer: From the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:18 commands the people to consider their situation starting from the 24th day of the ninth month when the foundation was laid, focusing on a fresh spiritual start.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:19, what promise does God make about blessing?
options: From this day, He will withhold blessings due to their sin
From this day, He will bless the people despite current unfruitfulness
Blessings will come only after the temple is finished
Blessings depend on the number of sacrifices offered
questions.correctAnswer: From this day, He will bless the people despite current unfruitfulness
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:19 promises that although the seed is not yet in the barn and trees have not borne fruit, from this day forward God will bless the people, indicating hope and renewal.

questions.question: What is the connection between Haggai 2:15 and Haggai 2:19 in teaching about obedience and blessing?
options: Reflecting on the past leads to despair and no blessing
Ignoring the temple foundation leads to blessings
Considering their past disobedience before the temple foundation prepares them to receive future blessing
Blessings come without any reflection or obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Considering their past disobedience before the temple foundation prepares them to receive future blessing
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:15 calls for reflection on their condition before the temple foundation, and Haggai 2:19 promises blessing from that point on, showing that recognition and repentance lead to restoration.

questions.question: How does Haggai 2:16 illustrate the practical consequences of the people's spiritual condition?
options: Their harvest and production were abundant
Their harvest and production were halved or less than expected
Their harvest was increased due to their faith
Their production was unaffected by their spiritual state
questions.correctAnswer: Their harvest and production were halved or less than expected
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:16 shows that yields were significantly less than expected, symbolizing how disobedience and uncleanness affected not just worship but daily life and prosperity.

questions.question: In Haggai 2:20-22, what future action does God promise concerning kingdoms and Zerubbabel?
options: God will establish Zerubbabel as king over all kingdoms without conflict
God will shake the heavens and earth, overthrow kingdoms, and make Zerubbabel a signet
God will destroy only the kingdom of Judah and ignore others
questions.correctAnswer: God will shake the heavens and earth, overthrow kingdoms, and make Zerubbabel a signet
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:20-22 promises God will shake the heavens and earth, overthrow kingdoms of heathen, and make Zerubbabel a signet, symbolizing divine authority and favor.

questions.question: What does being made a 'signet' mean for Zerubbabel according to Haggai 2:23?
options: He will be forgotten by God
He will be a symbol of God's chosen authority
He will lose his position as governor
He will become a high priest
questions.correctAnswer: He will be a symbol of God's chosen authority
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:23 indicates that making Zerubbabel a signet symbolizes God's chosen authority and approval, marking him as a key servant in His plan.

hard.title: Haggai Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Haggai Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2, what did the LORD say He would do to the heavens, earth, sea, and dry land?
questions.correctAnswer: Shake them
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:6 states, 'Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land;' indicating God will shake these elements.

questions.question: What is the significance of Zerubbabel according to Haggai 2:23?
options: He will be made as a signet, chosen by the LORD
He will rebuild the temple alone
He will be a prophet like Moses
He will lead the people into exile
questions.correctAnswer: He will be made as a signet, chosen by the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:23 says, 'I will take thee, O Zerubbabel... and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee,' highlighting his chosen status and role as a signet or seal of authority.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise concerning the glory of the latter temple compared to the former?
options: The glory of the latter house will be greater
The glory will be the same
The former house was more glorious
The latter house will have no glory
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of the latter house will be greater
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:9 states, 'The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former,' promising a surpassing glory for the rebuilt temple.

questions.question: What judgment did God say He had brought upon the people, according to Haggai 2:17?
options: Blasting, mildew, and hail in all the labors of their hands
questions.correctAnswer: Blasting, mildew, and hail in all the labors of their hands
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:17 describes God’s judgment as smiting them with 'blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands.'

questions.question: Which day and month did the word of the LORD come to Haggai commanding him to speak to Zerubbabel, according to Haggai 2:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventh month, twenty-first day
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:1 states, 'In the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month, came the word of the LORD by the prophet Haggai.'

questions.question: What question did Haggai ask concerning the holiness of objects touched by holy flesh, according to Haggai 2:12?
options: If holy flesh touches bread or wine, does it make them holy?
If unclean flesh touches holy vessels, are they unclean?
If holy water is spilled on the ground, is the ground holy?
If a priest touches unclean animals, are they holy?
questions.correctAnswer: If holy flesh touches bread or wine, does it make them holy?
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:12 asks, 'If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy?'

questions.question: True or False: According to Haggai 2:19, from the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, God promised to bless the people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:19 declares, 'From this day will I bless you,' marking the foundation day as the beginning of God's blessing.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Haggai 2:6-7 where God promises to shake the heavens and earth and fill the temple with glory?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism contrasting destruction and blessing
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 use parallelism contrasting God’s shaking of creation (judgment) with the promise to fill the temple with glory (blessing), highlighting divine sovereignty.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of God shaking the heavens and earth as a sign of divine judgment and restoration, similar to Haggai 2:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 12:26-27
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:26-27 references God's shaking of heaven and earth as a motif of judgment and establishing a new covenant, paralleling Haggai 2:21.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'signet' (Hebrew: chotam) used in Haggai 2:23 symbolize?
questions.correctAnswer: Authority and ownership
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chotam' means a signet ring, a mark of authority and ownership, symbolizing Zerubbabel's chosen role as God's representative (Haggai 2:23).

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:22, what will happen to the chariots, horses, and their riders?
options: They will come down, every one by the sword of his brother
They will be victorious in battle
They will be captured and enslaved
questions.correctAnswer: They will come down, every one by the sword of his brother
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states, '...the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother,' indicating internal destruction.

questions.question: Which Old Testament covenant is referenced in Haggai 2:5 when God says, 'According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt'?
questions.correctAnswer: The Mosaic Covenant
questions.explanation: The covenant mentioned relates to the Exodus, which is foundational to the Mosaic Covenant given at Sinai (Haggai 2:5).

questions.question: True or False: In Haggai 2:14, Haggai says the works of the people and what they offer are clean before the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:14 clearly states, 'and that which they offer there is unclean,' indicating impurity in their works and offerings.

questions.question: What is the immediate historical context of Haggai 2:10 referring to 'the second year of Darius'?
options: The Persian king Darius I's reign during the rebuilding of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The Persian king Darius I's reign during the rebuilding of the temple
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:10 refers to the period under Persian king Darius I when the temple rebuilding resumed after exile.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage can be connected to the promise of peace given in the temple area in Haggai 2:9?
questions.correctAnswer: John 14:27
questions.explanation: John 14:27 speaks of Jesus giving peace to His followers, echoing the peace promised by God in Haggai 2:9 for the temple area.

theological.title: Haggai Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Haggai Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:4 encourage Zerubbabel and Joshua to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and work
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:4 states, 'Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel... and be strong, O Joshua... and work: for I am with you.' This encourages them to remain strong and actively work on the temple despite their discouragement.

questions.question: According to Haggai 2:7, what will happen to the desire of all nations?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall come
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:7 mentions, 'And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come.' This indicates that the Lord will bring forth what is desired by the nations.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:9 say about the glory of the latter house?
options: It shall be less than the former
It shall be greater than the former
It will be the same as the former
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be greater than the former
questions.explanation: In Haggai 2:9, it states, 'The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former.' This prophecy indicates a future glory surpassing that of the first temple.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:8 declare about silver and gold?
questions.correctAnswer: They belong to the LORD
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:8 clearly states, 'The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.' This asserts God's sovereignty over material wealth.

questions.question: In Haggai 2:12, what do the priests say about holy flesh touching common food?
options: It does not make it holy
questions.correctAnswer: It does not make it holy
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:12 records the priests' response, 'No,' indicating that holy flesh does not sanctify common food items.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:14 indicate about the people and their offerings?
options: They are clean before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They are unclean
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:14 states, 'So is this people... and so is every work of their hands; and that which they offer there is unclean.' This highlights their spiritual state and the impurity of their offerings.

questions.question: What is the significance of the timing mentioned in Haggai 2:10?
options: It is the first month of the year
It is the ninth month of the second year of Darius
It is a day of fasting
It is the day of the temple's dedication
questions.correctAnswer: It is the ninth month of the second year of Darius
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:10 specifies, 'In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius,' marking a significant moment in the prophetic message.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:17 convey about the people's response to God's discipline?
questions.correctAnswer: They turned not to God
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:17 states, 'yet ye turned not to me, saith the LORD,' indicating the people's refusal to return to God after experiencing His discipline.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:19 promise regarding the blessings to the people?
options: They will be blessed from that day
questions.correctAnswer: They will be blessed from that day
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:19 promises, 'from this day will I bless you,' indicating a shift towards divine favor and blessings from God.

questions.question: How does Haggai 2:21 express God's sovereignty over kingdoms?
options: By shaking the heavens and the earth
questions.correctAnswer: By shaking the heavens and the earth
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:21 mentions, 'I will shake the heavens and the earth,' demonstrating God's authoritative control over all kingdoms and nations.

questions.question: In Haggai 2:23, how does God view Zerubbabel?
questions.correctAnswer: As a servant
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:23 refers to Zerubbabel as 'my servant,' indicating God's favor and intention to use him for His purposes.

questions.question: What does Haggai 2:16 reveal about the people's harvest?
questions.correctAnswer: It was diminished
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:16 illustrates, 'when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten,' showing that their productivity was significantly reduced due to their disobedience.

questions.question: What do Haggai 2:4 and 2:5 collectively teach about God's presence?
options: God's spirit remains among His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's spirit remains among His people
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:4 encourages strength and work, while 2:5 reassures that 'my spirit remaineth among you,' affirming God's continual presence and support.

questions.question: How do Haggai 2:6-7 and 2:22 relate to God's power over nations?
options: They reveal God will destroy earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: They reveal God will destroy earthly kingdoms
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:6-7 speaks of God shaking nations, while 2:22 states He will 'overthrow the throne of kingdoms,' emphasizing His supreme authority over all earthly powers.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in worldly affairs. What does Haggai 2:21-22 actually teach?
options: God actively shakes the heavens and the earth
questions.correctAnswer: God actively shakes the heavens and the earth
questions.explanation: Haggai 2:21-22 illustrates God's direct involvement in worldly affairs, stating, 'I will shake the heavens and the earth,' countering the sceptics' claim of divine indifference.
